newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. Newspaper Headlines - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. Newspaper Headlines - Nov 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- APPLE DAILY -- The Legislative Council passed a motion urging China to release jailed dissident Wang Dan.
-- HONG KONG DAILY NEWS -- The son of Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen had written a best-selling book called How To Go And Study In America. He spent six years in the United States.
-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS -- Administrative mistakes made by government departments wasted about $4 billion of public funds.

-- A research study shows Chinese university students see their perfect life as: being the boss of an international company, living in a castle-style house by the beach, and spending holidays skiing in Switzerland or driving madly on the highways of North America.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin congratulated U.S. President Bill Clinton on his re-election.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Investors were happy with the result of the U.S. presidential elections and sent Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index up to a new high of 12,775.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Dickson Concepts (International) plans to list ST Dupont on the Paris Bourse. Dupont's market value is estimated at about $1.7 billion.
SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- One of the architects of the U.S.-Hong Kong dollar peg urged mainland leaders to leave the Hong Kong dollar alone after the handover.
-- Weak market sentiment forced Shanghai power developer Shenergy Co to postpone indefinitely plans to issue what would have been the biggest B-share issue on the Shanghai stock exchange.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Hong Kong has pledged an ambitious programme of liberalisation in its individual action plan submitted to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.
